## Overview

Building and running containers on your computer requires a program known as a
container *runtime* to be installed. For this course, we use the runtime
provided by Podman since it

- is well supported across Windows, macOS and Linux
- has a mature graphical user interface (GUI), Podman Desktop
- is fully open source

The most widely used container project is *Docker*, which also
offers a graphical desktop application, Docker Desktop. However, unlike
Podman Desktop, it is not open source, and requires a paid license for use in
large commercial organisations. Importantly, container images built using Podman can be run using
Docker, and vice versa, since both support the Open Container Initiative (OCI)
standard.

::: {.callout-tip collapse=true}
## Secure by default

Podman led the way in security, since it was designed from the outset
to support rootless containers without requiring a privileged daemon, a process
that runs continually in the background of your system as an administrator.
Docker also now supports rootless containers, but this is harder to configure
and not used as standard.
:::

## Learning objectives

The purpose of this module is to install Podman Desktop only. If you already have
a working version of Podman Desktop installed, you can skip to [Module 1:
Introduction to Containers](../01-introduction/index.qmd).

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## Using Docker Desktop

Docker Desktop supports most of the same operations as Podman Desktop, so it can
be used to follow the course (note you'll have to translate the instructions for 
the Podman GUI into Docker Desktop equivalents). One exception is building container
images from a file, which Docker Desktop does not currently have an option for;
you will need to run [docker build](https://docs.docker.com/get-started/docker-concepts/building-images/build-tag-and-publish-an-image/)
from the command line.
:::
